[Pedagogy audit v2 · Applied automatically · New teaching] Question 10 requires working backwards from the range and the greatest value to find the missing least value, then reading it as a leaf. Nothing earlier teaches this, so a short worked step is needed first.
Worked example: **Stem**	**Leaf**
$2$	$N\;6$
$3$	$0\;7\;7$
$4$	$3$
$5$	$1\;9$

Key: $2\mid6$ means $26$

The range is $35$. Find the value of $N$.
The maximum is the last leaf of the last stem: $59$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=\text{maximum}-\text{minimum}\\35&=59-\text{minimum}\\\text{minimum}&=59-35\\\text{minimum}&=24\end{align*}$$

The minimum is the first leaf of the first stem, $2\mid N$, so $N=4$.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New teaching] Back-to-back plots first appear in questions 8 and 11 with no teaching. Add a short activity on reading them, including the leaf order on each side and combining both sides to find a statistic such as the median.
Worked example: $\def\arraystretch{1.4}\begin{array}{rr|c|lll}\multicolumn{2}{r|}{\mathrm{Boys}}&\mathrm{Stem}&\multicolumn{3}{l}{\mathrm{Girls}}\\\hline &6&1&2&5&\\8&3&2&1&4&7\\5&0&3&2&&\\7&1&4&3&&\end{array}$

Key: $2\mid4$ means $24$

Find the median of the results of all $14$ students.
Read each side outwards from the stem. Leaves are smallest next to the stem.

Boys: $16,\;23,\;28,\;30,\;35,\;41,\;47$

Girls: $12,\;15,\;21,\;24,\;27,\;32,\;43$

Order all $14$ results.

$12,\;15,\;16,\;21,\;23,\;24,\;27,\;28,\;30,\;32,\;35,\;41,\;43,\;47$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{14+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=7.5\end{align*}$$

The median is between the $7^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $8^{\mathrm{th}}$ scores.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{27+28}{2}\\\text{Median}&=27.5\end{align*}$$
